ImageDescription.value:
Grosnez Castle. Built around 1330 making use of the natural defences of the cliffs.
On the landward side the gatehouse was protected by two strong towers.

All that now remains is the arch and the bases of the walls.

Credit.value: From channel-islands.geographs.org; transferred by User:oxyman using geograph_org2commons.

Permission.value: Creative Commons Attribution Share-alike license 2.0

Categories.value: Taken with Canon EOS 450D|Grosnez Castle|Images from Geograph Channel Islands|Images by Bob Embleton|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation

ImageDescription.value:
Approaching Gros Nez Castle. The entrance archway is the main remaining structure.
The castle was probably demolished by the French Occupation forces between 1461 and 1468.

In the foreground is what appears to be a War Dept. boundary stone.

Credit.value: From channel-islands.geographs.org; transferred by User:oxyman using geograph_org2commons.

ImageDescription.value:
Gros Nez Castle natural defences. Thought to have been built by Sir John des Roches in about 1330.

It used the natural defences of the steep cliffs for three sides and a ditch with along the landward side where the locally quarried granite walls were thickest.
